items.title: OpenAI widened GPT-5.6 access
items.oneliner: OpenAI says GPT-5.6 now makes roughly 60% fewer factual errors, while free users get unlimited Luna text chats.

items.title: AI designed viable viruses from scratch
items.oneliner: Stanford and Arc used AI to create 16 working bacteriophages, making bio-design dramatically more useful and more dangerous.

items.title: DeepMind released WeatherNext 2 openly
items.oneliner: DeepMind says WeatherNext 2 adds a full day of cyclone warning lead time, with code and weights released.

items.title: Anthropic loosened biology safety filters
items.oneliner: Anthropic rewrote Fable 5's biology classifier to cut false positives, a reminder that safety work now directly shapes product utility.

items.title: Black market AI tokens are spreading
items.oneliner: Cheap stolen AI tokens are being resold at scale, turning API access into a security, billing, and data leakage problem.

items.title: GitHub Actions had a bad outage
items.oneliner: GitHub says stuck runner pods degraded Actions and Pages, and some workflow events could not be replayed automatically.

items.title: Meta lost a major child safety case
items.oneliner: A New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $567 million, showing platform safety failures are becoming balance-sheet events.

items.title: AMD bought model-in-silicon startup Taalas
items.oneliner: AMD bought Taalas after a 16,960 tokens-per-second demo, betting model-specific chips can undercut GPU inference economics.

items.title: Inference routing is becoming product moat
items.oneliner: Cursor says its router is trained on millions of interactions, signaling that model selection logic is now core infrastructure.

items.title: DeepSeek pricing pressure is surfacing
items.oneliner: Reports of DeepSeek API price hikes suggest the era of subsidized inference is ending faster than many app teams planned.
